page.title: Best Virtual Events Platforms: A Buyer's Guide
page.description: Learn how to choose between self-serve streaming, webinar software, and enterprise event suites. Compare cost models and production requirements.
page.h1: How do I choose the best virtual events platform?
page.definition: Best virtual events platforms are software solutions used to host digital gatherings, ranging from simple self-serve streaming studios to complex enterprise event suites. These tools manage attendee registration, live broadcast delivery, and interactive engagement features, serving as the technical foundation for webinars, summits, and hybrid conferences.
page.quick_answer: Select a platform based on your event scale: use self-serve tools like StreamYard for simple broadcasts, Zoom Webinars for moderated sessions, or enterprise suites like Cvent or Bizzabo for large-scale conferences.

sections.h2: What are the different types of virtual event platforms?

blocks.p: Platforms fall into three main categories based on technical complexity and intended audience scale. You must match the tool to your specific event format to avoid overpaying for features you will not use.

sections.h2: How much do virtual event platforms cost?

blocks.p: Pricing depends on whether you need a simple monthly subscription or a customized enterprise contract. Most providers use one of three distinct commercial structures.

ul: Per-host licences sized by attendee capacity, such as Zoom Webinars
Self-serve monthly plans, such as StreamYard or Livestorm
Annual contracts quoted by sales, such as ON24, Cvent, Bizzabo, or Goldcast

sections.h2: What is the difference between a platform and production?

blocks.p: The platform is the software, while production is the human and technical labor required to run the show. You must budget for both separately to ensure a professional outcome.

ol: Purchase the platform software for hosting and registration
Hire a production crew to manage the run of show and technical execution
Secure a backup stream to prevent downtime during live segments
Schedule a full rehearsal on the real platform two to five days before the event
Conduct a technical check sixty minutes before going live

sections.h2: How do I manage the workstreams for a large summit?

blocks.p: Large-scale events require dividing responsibilities across specific workstreams to ensure nothing is missed. A summit needs six to eight weeks of management, whereas a webinar needs three to four.

sections.h2: What tools should I use for event operations?

blocks.p: Successful event execution relies on a stack of specialized tools for planning, publishing, and reporting. Using integrated tools reduces manual hand-offs and errors.

ul: Asana, Monday.com, or Airtable for the event calendar and workflow
Google Docs or Notion for writing briefs
WordPress, Webflow, or HubSpot for publishing event landing pages
GA4 and HubSpot for post-event reporting and lead tracking

faq.q: How much does professional event production cost?
faq.a: Moderated webinars typically range from $2,500 to $7,500 per production. For larger executive summits, online conferences, or hybrid productions, costs range from $10,000 to $50,000 and above. West Peek Productions produces virtual, hybrid and webinar events and sets up marketing, content and creative operations, but does not sell software.

faq.q: When should I start planning my virtual event?
faq.a: You should plan a hybrid conference six to eight weeks in advance. For a standard webinar, a lead time of three to four weeks is realistic. You must lock in your venue AV and your chosen platform before your event agenda is finalized to avoid scheduling conflicts.

faq.q: What happens after the live event ends?
faq.a: You should send the event replay to your attendees within 24 to 48 hours while the content is still fresh in their minds. Use tools like HubSpot or GA4 to analyze attendee engagement and convert that attention into an owned audience of email subscribers.

faq.q: Can I use my existing software for a summit?
faq.a: Yes, professional productions can be run on the platforms you already use, such as Zoom Webinars, Microsoft Teams, ON24, or StreamYard. The production crew brings the technical expertise, including the run of show, speaker rehearsals, and backup streams, regardless of which software you select.
